title: Cheapest-correct model evaluation benchmark for Muse Spark 1.1
description: A standardized, reproducible cross-model benchmark packet and provider adapter are required to evaluate whether Muse Spark 1.1 should be promoted into the model-routing stack. The evaluation must pass correctness, safety, privacy, latency, reliability, and governance gates before the 'cheapest correct model wins' doctrine applies. The benchmark includes MCP reliability, governed delegation, repository execution, long-context integrity, computer-use safety, and cost-adjusted correctness tests. The final disposition must be one of REJECTED, BOUNDED_USE, or PROMOTED_WITH_SCOPE.
pain_point: Without a structured benchmark, reliance on vendor claims and lack of standardized cross-model comparison make it impossible to reliably determine the cheapest correct model. This risks promoting models that fail safety, privacy, or reliability gates, or missing cost-saving opportunities. Current default routes may not be optimal because they are not backed by systematic evidence.
use_case: Evaluating Muse Spark 1.1 for integration into the HUMMBL/Ownward model-routing stack. The task requires building a provider-isolated adapter, a provider-policy declaration, and running fixed benchmark tasks against Muse and comparison models (GPT-5.6 Luna/Terra/Sol, Claude Fable 5, current promoted free/local lane) using identical inputs, success criteria, and tool permissions. The goal is to produce an evidence packet supporting exactly one disposition.

title: Keep notes short for AI tooling readability
description: Ensure the latest notes are short enough for ChatGPT/Codex to read the full text, preserving exact note text and context before any agent acts.
pain_point: If the inbox grows too long or starts truncating, the AI tooling cannot read the full note text, which may cause loss of information before agents act.
use_case: User needs to manage HVAC review inbox so that AI tooling can read the latest note text completely, with attached metadata like page label, route, URL, viewport, user agent, priority, kind, and visible context.

title: No first-party way to view a generated PDF in sandbox
description: When an agent generates a PDF (or other document artifact) inside a sandbox run, there is no built-in command to preview it. The agent must manually rasterize the PDF to PNG via a second sandbox invocation using pdftoppm, then Read each PNG to visually verify the output. This adds extra sandbox round-trips, increases wall-clock time, and creates throwaway files that auto-sync to the project and must be manually cleaned up. The same friction applies to all sandbox-generated document artifacts (PDF, docx, etc.).
pain_point: No first-party PDF viewer — agent must rasterize its own deliverable to see it, adding a full sandbox round-trip and manual cleanup of auto-synced intermediate artifacts. 'Every sandbox-generated document artifact (PDF, docx, etc.) will hit this same wall.'
use_case: Agent runs a one-off data task (CSV in, PDF report out) via `gipity sandbox run`. After generating the PDF, the agent wants to visually confirm the layout before calling the task done. Since no platform command exists, it hand-rolls a second sandbox invocation: `pdftoppm -png -r 90 docs/sales-report.pdf docs/preview` to rasterize pages, then `Read` on each PNG. After fixing a chart, it must repeat the entire rasterize-and-Read cycle.

title: Autonomous run log and push notification for queue execution tracking
description: Users need a system that automatically posts summary comments for each queue execution to a pinned tracking issue, enabling push notifications via GitHub app for real-time monitoring. This is currently implemented as a pinned tracking issue for the Fable ↔ CLI autonomous crank loop.
pain_point: Without this automated logging, Alex would not receive immediate push notifications about queue execution status, potentially missing critical updates or failures in the autonomous crank loop.
use_case: Tracking queue execution progress in a GitHub issue, where each queue run posts a formatted comment with ISO timestamp, items statuses (shipped/blocked/skipped), commits, CI status, and branch head, to receive push notifications for status updates.

title: Deterministic step of game loop for verifying real-time canvas games
description: The AI agent built a Phaser brick-breaker game and attempted to verify the real gameplay loop (ball bounces, bricks break, score increments, lives decrement) by driving the deployed page with `gipity page eval`. The platform returned a warning that the page painted at 14.5 fps, that waiting on real wall-clock time advances the physics far slower than it appears, and that the agent should instead 'step the app's own loop deterministically'. However, nothing in the CLI or the skills gives the agent a way to step a running game loop. The agent had no follow-up move: it dropped real-time verification entirely, took a static screenshot, read the PNG, and shipped the game with its core mechanic never exercised. This is a recurring issue for any canvas/physics/animation app on the platform.
pain_point: The platform only provides real-time wall-clock execution for `page eval`, which at 14.5 fps advances physics too slowly to trigger collisions and score changes within reasonable time. The warning advises 'step the app's own loop deterministically' but the CLI and skills offer no mechanism to step a running game loop, forcing the agent to abandon verification of the core gameplay mechanics entirely.
use_case: Agent built a Phaser brick-breaker and tried to verify the real gameplay loop (ball bounces, bricks break, score increments, lives decrement) by driving the deployed page with `gipity page eval`. First two evals worked (sampled ball position over time), but on the third eval — the one that would have confirmed a brick collision and a score change — the platform warned of slow render (14.5 fps) and suggested stepping the app's own loop deterministically. Agent had no tool to do that, so it abandoned verification, took a static screenshot, and shipped without exercising brick collision, scoring, lives, or win/game-over screens.

use_case: Maya (Home Baker) and Fatima (Food Cart Operator) rely on direct messages to capture demand, confirm orders, and coordinate pickups. Currently, WhatsApp messages are disconnected from OHC, requiring them to constantly switch between personal/business WhatsApp and OHC.

title: 基于 capability 的 native fan-out lifecycle 契约

pain_point: 문서대로 실행한 것이 실패한다 (按照文档执行会失败)：FULL reviewer 4개를 한 batch로 띄우거나 없는 close를 호출하면 문서대로 실행한 것이 실패한다，即文档假设的 lifecycle 和 slot 数与实际 surface 不一致，导致操作无法正确完成。
use_case: 开发者使用 Direct Codex 进行 multi-agent 操作时，按照文档预设的 spawn_agent → wait_agent → close_agent 和 6 threads 执行，但实际 CLI surface 是 spawn_agent, send_message, followup_task, wait_agent, interrupt_agent, list_agents 且没有 explicit close，同时当前 session 只广告 root 包含 active slot 4 个，导致文档与实际 surface 不匹配，执行失败。期望结果是文档中的 lifecycle 和 slot 契约能根据实际 CLI surface 动态调整，通过 capability probe 选择 current 或 legacy profile。

title: Replace boolean tool outcomes with native error semantics
description: Remove the boolean 'ok' field from KhalaToolResult and use a closed union of success { summary, data? } and failure { summary, error } with stable error codes like 'invalid_issue_packet'. This ensures validation failures are correctly signaled without duplicating success state, reduces visual burden, and allows collapsed Pi rendering to show native success/error styling.
pain_point: The current boolean 'ok' field duplicates success state, treats validation failure as success (since both conforming and nonconforming packets are reported as successful tool executions), and adds visual burden by serializing the full envelope into visible tool content, resulting in verbose JSON output even for simple validations.
use_case: In the Pi runtime integration, refactor Khala tool results to use native error semantics instead of a boolean 'ok' field. Specifically, khala_triage.validate should return success for conforming rich/legacy packets and return failure with the stable 'invalid_issue_packet' error code and ordered structural violations for partial, empty, or mixed-schema packets. Collapsed Pi rendering should show a concise native success/error line instead of pretty-printed result JSON, while expanded/model-visible representations retain structured action data for follow-up tasks.

pain_point: 如果关闭该issue，将会丢失代理的咨询分析记录，影响系统对代码的持续监控和质量反馈。
use_case: 维护者在低ACMM级别时，代理仅发布分析结果而不创建issue或PR，需要有一个持续开放的issue来收集这些结果，并通过govner发布定期摘要评论。

title: Align VoltAgent API with ai-sdk v7 as an outer framework
description: VoltAgent should become an outer framework around ai-sdk instead of a hidden abstraction layer. The primary API must reuse ai-sdk names, options, semantics, and types, with VoltAgent-specific features under a `voltagent` namespace. This avoids semantic drift, duplicated types, and blocked access to newer ai-sdk capabilities.
pain_point: Current wrappers (`agent.generateText(input, options)`) create semantic drift from ai-sdk, require hand-written parallel types (`BaseGenerationOptions`, `maxSteps`, `stop`, `Tool`), block access to newer ai-sdk features (like `Output.object`), and cause version lag (peers ai:^6.0.0 vs ai-sdk v7 source).
use_case: Framework author wants to redesign VoltAgent vNext to expose ai-sdk-native API (e.g., `agent.generateText({ prompt, temperature, voltagent: {...} })`) instead of proprietary wrappers like `agent.generateText(input, options)`, while preserving VoltAgent's value-add (workflows, memory, observability).

The need is to update the OpenAPI specification to accurately reflect the actual API surface.
pain_point: Significant gaps between the @directus/specs package and the actual REST API surface; undocumented endpoints have no spec coverage, causing confusion and integration issues; incorrect query parameters and missing methods hinder API usability and adoption.
use_case: Systematic review of controller routes in api/src/controllers/ against spec paths in packages/specs/src/paths/ to catalog every gap found so far and achieve manageable spec coverage.

title: Switch execution context to Dedicated Workers in mcp-server
description: User requests a feature in mcp-server to replicate Chrome DevTools' ability to switch the execution context to dedicated workers. This would allow AI agents to interact with worker global scope, e.g., running commands like `Neo.get('my-component-id')` to inspect live objects, which is currently impossible because mcp-server is bound to the main thread.
pain_point: The mcp-server is bound to the main thread's execution context, making it impossible to interact with a worker's global scope. For example, the user cannot run `Neo.get('my-component-id')` to inspect a live object that exists only within the worker, because error messages from workers may bubble up but cannot be interactively queried.
use_case: Integrating mcp-server into the Neo.mjs framework workflow for an AI development agent (Gemini 2.5 Pro) to 'see' and interact with the UI. The framework uses an OMT architecture where most application logic runs inside workers. User needs to debug by switching execution context to a specific worker and evaluating Runtime commands in that worker's scope.

title: 修复 gh shim 递归选择另一个 aidevops shim 的缺陷
description: 当 PATH 上存在两个 aidevops gh shim（immutable runtime-bundle shim 和 mutable installed shim）且都在原生 gh 之前时，`_find_real_gh()` 函数仅排除自身目录，导致 runtime-bundle shim 选择 installed shim，而 installed shim 又选择 runtime-bundle shim，形成递归调用直至超时。此缺陷阻塞 issue 读取、PR 操作、诊断等所有依赖 gh 的功能，且紧急绕过 `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1` 也因使用同一有缺陷的解析器而失效。需要修复 shim 的解析逻辑，使其只调用一次原生 gh，并确保紧急绕过也能正常生效。
pain_point: 两个 aidevops gh shim 递归选择对方，导致 `gh` 命令超时且退出码 124，阻塞 issue 读取、PR 操作、诊断、pulse routines 和框架助手；紧急绕过 `AIDEVOPS_GH_SHIM_DISABLE=1` 同样超时，无法绕开；用户被迫手动使用 `/usr/bin/gh` 或清理 PATH，但框架助手仍易受攻击。
use_case: 在 long-running session 中，PATH 以 immutable runtime-bundle agents/scripts 开头，随后是 mutable installed agents/scripts，最后是原生 gh。运行 `gh --version` 或任何 gh 命令（如 `gh issue view`）时，shim 递归调用导致命令超时，需要修复 shim 使其直接调用原生 gh。

title: Multi-Agent Coordination Health Monitor with Deadlock Detection
description: Build a real-time monitor that tracks agent task completion, detects stuck agents, identifies coordination bottlenecks (deadlocks, blocking, idle agents), and triggers auto-recovery (task reassignment, agent restart, or escalation to PM agent) to reduce coordination-related failures by 40%+ in multi-agent test scenarios.
pain_point: Coordination-related failures in multi-agent pipelines due to deadlocks, blocking, and idle agents that are invisible in single-agent testing, leading to stuck workflows and reduced reliability; no existing monitor to detect circular blocking or consistently slow agents, and no automatic recovery mechanisms.

title: System prompt tool name mismatch: query_multimodal_ai vs query_multimodal_api
description: The SYSTEM_PROMPT in config.py:198 refers to the tool as 'query_multimodal_ai', but the MCP tool is registered as 'query_multimodal_api' in mcp_server.py:98. This causes the model to emit an invalid tool call, leading to extra correction iterations or failed vision analysis. The fix is to align the prompt text with the actual registered tool name.
pain_point: The model emits a tool call named query_multimodal_ai after a camera-snapshot tool; the call fails with 'unknown tool', costing an extra correction iteration per turn (or a failed vision analysis on models that don't retry), particularly on smaller local models that trust prompt text over the tool schema list.
use_case: Developer running a multi-agent code audit discovers that the system prompt instructs the model to call 'query_multimodal_ai', but the tool exposed via MCP is named 'query_multimodal_api'. The model follows the prompt literally, causing tool call failures.

ChatMemory maintains conversation history, but during confirmation, the short/generic input does not allow tool selection logic to infer what tool to call or what operation to complete. Additionally, multiple follow-up or unexpected clarification questions (e.g., 'change the name', 'what email did I give?') become difficult to manage because a single tool must handle all such queries after initial invocation. The user seeks best practices or design patterns to manage follow-up confirmations without re-triggering tool filtering and losing original intent context.
